items.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025
items.q: And you know I always liked going to hear them play whenever I could and I told them, you know if you ever need a drummer, you know try me out.

ctx.x: And how does that work? You get a recommendation? Somebody recommends you, you happen to cross paths on Fifth Avenue or how does that thing occur?

I was still living in Los Angeles and it was actually that year that Gary called me to play. I was with George Shearing that year, it was the best paying job in jazz. And you know the guys in the more — let’s say less commercial jazz groups were all envious of me and I knew them all, because I made twice as much money as they did, working with George. But I just — you know we didn’t get to play real hard, I did a lot of brushes which was good for me. I learned to play the brushes very well I think. Over the ‘60s…
Oh that’s a great one. I had a question down the road, advice to students, and you just nailed it. Do you ever tell them be aware of what bass player you’re joining?
